subject: Our World and Our People
name: Basic 2 Our World and Our People
description: The Basic 2 OWOP curriculum continues to nurture honest, creative, and responsible citizens. It focuses on understanding God as the Sustainer of life, self-identity, family roles, environmental cleanliness, weather elements, map making, and religious values through worship and festivals.

strands.title: ALL ABOUT US
strands.description: Deepening understanding of God, self-identity, family roles, and obedience to rules.

subStrands.title: Nature of God
subStrands.description: Understanding God as the Sustainer of life.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the attributes of God

indicators.description: Mention the attributes of God that reveal His nature as Sustainer of life

exemplars.description: Learners mention the attributes of God as sustainer of life: Giver of rain and sunshine, The One who makes plants grow, The Giver of air.
Learners mention these attributes of God in their local languages.
Learners talk about the attributes of God relevant to their daily lives, e.g. God gives life, rain and air.

imagePrompts.prompt: A peaceful outdoor scene showing nature's gifts: rain falling on green plants, the sun shining brightly, and children breathing in fresh air. The children look happy and thankful.

subStrands.title: Myself
subStrands.description: Developing a sense of self-identity and worth.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of self as a unique individual

indicators.description: Identify things to do to develop a sense of self identity and self-worth

exemplars.description: Learners talk about themselves individually and appreciate the way God created them e.g. "I am black and beautiful, I like the way God created me. I have great qualities".
Learners role play scenarios and engage in activities that teach them the importance of developing a strong self-identity.
Learners compose poems/write essays about themselves and what they can do to feel more valued at home, school and the community.

imagePrompts.prompt: A confident Ghanaian child standing in front of a mirror or peers, smiling and gesturing to themselves, expressing pride in their appearance and abilities. Diverse friends cheer them on.

subStrands.title: My Family and the Community
subStrands.description: Appreciating roles and responsibilities within the family.

contentStandards.description: Show appreciation of the roles of members of the family in their daily lives

indicators.description: Identify the role and responsibilities of the individual members of the family

exemplars.description: Learners, in groups, talk about their roles and roles of their parents in the family: Parents: Provision of shelter, food, security and education. Children: running errands, performing house chores, etc.
Learners role play the functions of the various members in the family, e.g. learners play the role of a father, mother, etc.

imagePrompts.prompt: A detailed family scene in a Ghanaian home. A father is repairing a bicycle or reading, a mother is cooking or helping with homework, and children are sweeping the compound or fetching water.

subStrands.title: Home and School
subStrands.description: Understanding the importance of obeying rules.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the need to obey rules

indicators.description: Explain the need for obeying rules in the home and school

exemplars.description: Learners work in groups to talk about rules in the home, school and community.
Learners role play scenarios on obeying rules in the home, school and community.
Learners compose rhymes on obeying rules in the home and school

imagePrompts.prompt: A classroom scene where children are following rules: walking in a line, raising hands to speak, and tidying up books. A poster on the wall lists 'Class Rules' with simple pictures.

strands.title: ALL AROUND US
strands.description: Exploring the environment, plants, animals, mapping, and population.

subStrands.title: The Environment and the Weather
subStrands.description: Keeping the environment clean and understanding weather elements.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of keeping the environment clean and safe

indicators.description: Describe ways of making the environment clean and safe

exemplars.description: Take a nature walk of the school environment and observe things in the environment-man made and natural: water, trees, stones, animals, buildings, cars, tables, chairs, etc.
Learners talk about things they can do to make the environment clean and safe e.g. planting trees, proper waste disposal, avoid bush burning, avoid defecating in water bodies, legal mining.
Learners demonstrate safe practices in the community, e.g. sweeping school compound, picking litter.

imagePrompts.prompt: Children actively cleaning their school compound. Some are sweeping with local brooms, others are picking up litter into a bin, and one group is planting a small tree.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of elements of the weather

exemplars.description: Learners explain the elements of weather, e.g. temperature, rainfall/precipitation, humidity, wind and cloud cover.
Learners draw weather chart using symbols.
Learners watch videos or pictures of different weather conditions.

imagePrompts.prompt: A classroom weather station. A child is changing a weather chart on the wall to show 'Sunny' and 'Windy' symbols. Other children are looking out the window observing the sky.

subStrands.title: Plants and Animals
subStrands.description: Recognising important plants and animals in the community.

contentStandards.description: Recognise important plants and animals in the community

indicators.description: Explore the important plants in the community

exemplars.description: Learners identify and talk about crops like cocoa, yam, maize, shea butter, etc, and talk about why they are important to the community.
Learners draw and colour the important crops in their community

imagePrompts.prompt: A montage of important Ghanaian crops: a cocoa tree with pods, a maize plant, and a yam mound with vines. A child is standing next to one, admiring it.

indicators.description: Explore the important animals in the community

exemplars.description: Learners mention some domestic animals in the community and talk about why they are important
Learners observe some of the animals in the community and how people take care of them

imagePrompts.prompt: A child feeding domestic animals in a village setting. There are chickens pecking grain, a goat tied nearby, and a sheep. The scene shows care for animals.

subStrands.title: Map Making and Land Marks
subStrands.description: Sketching and locating things in the classroom.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the skills needed to map the environment

indicators.description: Sketch and locate things in the classroom

exemplars.description: Sketch and colour the shape of the classroom, e.g. Square, Rectangle, Round.
Through questions and answers, guide learners to indicate where they sit in the classroom, on their sketches with a small round shape.
Learners show on their sketches the location of the following: Chalk/White board (Bb/Wb), Cupboard (C), Teacher's table (Tt).

imagePrompts.prompt: A bird's-eye view sketch of a classroom layout on a chalkboard. It shows the teacher's desk at the front, rows of student desks, and a cupboard at the back, labeled with simple abbreviations.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate basic understanding of population changes

indicators.description: Explain the need to accept and adapt to a change in the total number of people, as a responsible citizen

exemplars.description: Learners role play problems of a large family size.
Represent the number of family members in your house with a bar chart.
Explain what happens to the class size when a new learner joins or leaves your class.

imagePrompts.prompt: A classroom scene welcoming a new student. The teacher introduces a new boy or girl to the class, illustrating a change in class population. A simple chart on the wall shows class numbers.

strands.title: OUR BELIEFS AND VALUES
strands.description: Exploring worship, festivals, human rights, and leadership.

subStrands.title: Worship
subStrands.description: Appreciating the importance of religious worship.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the importance of religious worship

exemplars.description: Take learners to a place of worship such as the church, mosque or the shrine to observe the mode of worship or show pictures videos of the various modes of worship.
Learners role play demonstrate/talk about the importance of worship at home, school, church/mosque/shrine.

imagePrompts.prompt: A respectful montage showing children at different places of worship: singing in a church, praying in a mosque, and observing a traditional ceremony. They look reverent and peaceful.

subStrands.title: Festivals
subStrands.description: Understanding festivals and family roles in religion.

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of festivals celebrated in Ghana

indicators.description: Describe activities which take place during the celebration of festivals

exemplars.description: Learners talk about festivals they have witnessed (Islam, Christianity, Traditional).
Learners role play activities that take place during the festivals: merry-making, sharing, family re-union, worship, etc.

imagePrompts.prompt: A festive scene showing a traditional festival durbar with a chief in a palanquin, drummers, and dancers. People are cheering and celebrating.

contentStandards.description: Investigate the roles of the family and community in their daily lives

indicators.description: Identify things that families do to show their commitment to God

exemplars.description: Learners talk about the religious activities their families perform to show commitment to God: morning devotion, going to church, mosque or the shrine.
Learners role play what their families do to show commitment to God, e.g. worship, offertory, Sadaqah, Zakat, prayer and fasting.

imagePrompts.prompt: A family gathered for morning devotion in their living room, heads bowed in prayer. Another scene showing a family walking together to a place of worship.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of human rights as a citizen

indicators.description: Explain the importance of respecting the rights of others

exemplars.description: Learners talk about the importance of allowing others to enjoy their rights, e.g. peace, cooperation, teamwork
Learners role-play ways of allowing others to enjoy their rights e.g. tolerance, love, respect, etc

imagePrompts.prompt: Two children peacefully sharing a book or toy, demonstrating respect for each other's rights. Another scene shows children waiting their turn in a queue.

contentStandards.description: Narrate the early life stories of the leaders of the three main religions in Ghana

indicators.description: Narrate the story of the early life of the religious leaders in the three religions in Ghana

exemplars.description: Learners mention the names of the religious leaders: Jesus Christ, the Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.), Okomfo Anokye, Toha Zie, etc.
Learners role play some important aspects of the early life of a religious leader.
Learners explain how they will apply the moral lessons from the religious leaders in their daily lives.

imagePrompts.prompt: A child dressed in simple costume role-playing a young religious leader (like Jesus in the temple or young Muhammad). Other children sit and listen attentively.
